messages:
Ada: Heads up — seeing CA thrash on us-west1 gpu-nodepool. Nodes spin up to handle queued jobs, then ~4–6m later CA marks them unneeded and drains; a bunch of pods fail to evict and we end up re-queuing. Observed ~30% wasted GPU time this morning. Anyone else?

Ben: Can you paste the autoscaler events/logs from the last hour? Which --expander are we on?

Ada: We use binpacking currently. Snip from autoscaler log:```I0308 09:12:02.123456 1 autoscaler.go:123] ScaleUp: adding 2 nodes to nodegroup gpu-usw1-pool (pending scheduling)
I0308 09:16:55.654321 1 scale_down.go:234] Node gpu-node-12 unneeded for 5m0s, attempting to remove
I0308 09:16:55.654378 1 drain.go:98] drain failed: 7 pods blocked (cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict not set), 3 pods have PDBs
I0308 09:19:00.000000 1 autoscaler.go:315] ScaleUp: adding 1 node to nodegroup gpu-usw1-pool (backoff)```

devops-bot: [autoscaler] Event: InstanceGroup gpu-usw1-pool: scale-up->scale-down flapping detected (count=3)

Rafael: Hm. Two likely causes: (1) pods without the CA-safe-to-evict annotation (long-running batch jobs and some GPUs) and (2) DaemonSets/local-storage or PDBs preventing eviction. GPU driver DS uses hostPath and is showing up as a system pod — that's expected but prevents removal unless CA is configured to ignore daemonset usage.

Claire: binpacking is aggressive for packing GPUs and can increase fragmentation if node groups differ. For multi-nodepools with mixed shapes it's sometimes better to switch to --expander=least-waste or use priority expander with priorities per nodegroup so cheap preemptible pools are preferred for burst. Also enable --balance-similar-node-groups to avoid draining the same AZ repeatedly.

Ada: Proposed quick changes to trial in staging:```--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--max-node-provision-time=15m
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false
--ignore-daemonsets-utilization=false```And we will annotate batch pods that are restart-safe with:
`cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "true"`

Ben: Increasing scale-down-unneeded-time to 20m will reduce flapping but obviously increases cost. Can you rough-cost that change?

Rafael: Quick napkin: avg GPU node cost (on our reserved/mix) ~ $4.20/hr. If we keep 6 extra nodes on average during peak windows because of longer unneeded-time, cost delta ~ 6 * 4.2 = $25.2/hr during the affected 3hr window (~$75/day). But current waste from retries + failed drains looks comparable given lost GPU minutes. We should run this in staging for 24h and measure.

Sasha: Also checking region constraints — us-west1 has periodic capacity pressure for certain GPU SKUs. CA sometimes launches a fallback in us-central1 which violates affinity rules and causes more churn. Can we add a small buffer pool (1–2 nodes) in each region pinned for burst so CA doesn't try cross-region?

Claire: Another small win: set annotation on batch controller templates so pods are evictable by default, and add a pre-delete hook for long-running jobs to checkpoint. For driver DS, we can mark driver pods as DaemonSet but CA flag --ignore-daemonsets-utilization=false will ensure daemonsets don't block removal unless significant.

Ada: Plan: 1) Apply proposed CA flags to staging cluster tomorrow 09:00 UTC. 2) Add safe-to-evict annotation to job templates and a migration for currently running tasks. 3) Add a 1-node regional buffer pool in us-west1 and us-central1 for 48h canary. 4) Measure scale events and GPU utilization, revert if cost delta > 2x current waste.

Ben: Sounds reasonable. +1 for the staging run. Please add the flag diff to the PR and set a 24h rollback timer.

Rafael: I'll help with the cost dashboard query (query will show wasted GPU-minutes caused by failed drains).

Ada: Thanks — will open PR and ping when the staging roll is live.

Sasha: One more note — watch for kubelet/network flaps causing nodes to briefly report NotReady which CA sees as unschedulable; we should check calico/kube-proxy logs in parallel during the run.

Ada: Good call. I'll add network checks to the runbook.

(threads end)
